lessons: CRITICAL fix: the headline nikud-insensitive search recipe was FALSE -- unaccent does NOT strip Hebrew nikud (only Latin/Greek combining marks U+0300-U+0362; the Hebrew points block U+0591-U+05C7 is untouched, so unaccent('שָׁלוֹם') returns it unchanged). Replaced with an IMMUTABLE strip_nikud() using regexp_replace over [U+0591-U+05C7], plus a verify-it-strips assertion. Fixed in SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md.

Correctness: is_israeli_business_hours marked IMMUTABLE but AT TIME ZONE on timestamptz is STABLE (depends on tzdata) -> changed to STABLE (EN+HE). pgcrypto 'for UUID generation' is obsolete since gen_random_uuid() is in core PG13+ -> noted in supabase-israel-patterns.md. Over-strict single-column phone CHECK rejected 1-700/1-800 and 07X VoIP -> loosened + told readers to do exact validation in the app layer (EN+HE). Corrected the collation guide's wrong claim that non-deterministic ICU folds sofit (final) letters -- it does not; it equalizes nikud, not base-letter final forms. Added a PostgreSQL 13+ version baseline note.

Expert+Judge round 2: PROPAGATED the unaccent->strip_nikud fix everywhere it had leaked through (Example 1 EN+HE, workflow step 3, the no-stemmer gotcha, AND scripts/hebrew-search-setup.sql which had built search_vector/queries with no nikud stripping) -- a fix is not done until every example and shipped script matches the prose. Also CORRECTED my own wrong collation edit: the Judge ran PG 17.6 and showed default he-IL-x-icu does NOT equalize nikud, and sofit is a TERTIARY (not primary) variant -- so there is no strength that folds nikud but keeps sofit; nikud-insensitivity must come from strip_nikud(), not the collation. Rewrote the collation guide + evidence accordingly and noted non-deterministic collations can't back UNIQUE/btree/LIKE. Disclosed the Hebrew no-stemmer recall gap (prefix clitics) and to lean on pg_trgm.

Deferred (MAJOR, next cycle): Hebrew FTS has no stemming/lemmatization, so prefixes (ו/ב/כ/ל/ה/מ/ש) and plurals make 'ספר'/'הספר'/'ספרים' distinct lexemes -- document the recall workaround (prefix-stripping normalization or trigram fallback as a recall strategy, not just typo tolerance). Deferred (MINOR): single jsonb {he,en} bilingual-content pattern + indexing; ILIKE vs trigram decision guide; BOI no-rate-on-weekend carry-forward guard.

CRITICAL (version regression): PostgreSQL 18 ALLOWS LIKE on non-deterministic collations ('These used to generate an error', PG18 release notes). The skill asserted the opposite in 4 places including a whole Troubleshooting entry keyed to an error message that no longer fires on the version the skill itself declares current. Replaced with a per-version operator matrix; ILIKE and regex DO still error (verified on 18.6), and LIKE is filter-only with no prefix index.

CRITICAL: search_hebrew() never matched English. The vector stems English columns with the 'english' config ('invoice' stored as 'invoic') while every query used plainto_tsquery('simple'), so no English query could ever match. Nobody had reported this. Fixed by OR-ing both tsquery configs. Lesson: when a generated column mixes two text-search configurations, the QUERY must mix them too, and a bilingual search function needs an explicit test per language.

CRITICAL: the body trigram index was dead. search_hebrew()'s fuzzy branch only touched title_he, so idx_..._body_he_trgm was never used and a document containing 'והחשבונית' was not returned for 'חשבונית'. Deeper lesson learned the hard way this cycle: the first fix used `%` semantics and `coalesce(body_he,'')`, and BOTH were wrong. `%` is whole-string similarity and is diluted by column length (0.067 on a 104-char body vs word_similarity 0.750), and wrapping the column in coalesce() defeats a plain-column index (proved: Seq Scan under enable_seqscan=off). Match the EXACT expression the index was built on.

CRITICAL, self-inflicted and caught only by running it: each pg_trgm operator reads its OWN GUC with a DIFFERENT default (% -> similarity_threshold 0.3, <% -> word_similarity_threshold 0.6, <<% -> strict 0.5). The first version of the <% fix set only similarity_threshold, so the new branch stayed gated at 0.6 and was inert. Feeding one caller value into all three was also wrong (word_similarity runs much higher, so 0.2 there returns near-unrelated rows). Resolved with two separate parameters carrying the operators' own defaults.

CRITICAL, also self-inflicted: the 'fixed' nikud class [U+0591-U+05C7 plus singletons] still spanned the whole block, so the first regexp_replace deleted U+05BE MAQAF before the second pass could turn it into a space, and 'תל־אביב' indexed as the single lexeme 'תלאביב'. Only an end-to-end search test caught it. The block contains four NON-mark codepoints (05BE Pd, 05C0/05C3/05C6 Po); the correct Mn-only class is [U+0591-U+05BD, U+05BF, U+05C1-U+05C2, U+05C4-U+05C5, U+05C7]. Never approximate a Unicode class by block range when the block is mixed-category.

CRITICAL: Israeli acronyms were unsearchable. The default FTS parser classifies gershayim U+05F4 as a BLANK, so 'בע"מ' tokenises as 'בע' + 'מ' while users type 'בעמ' (ts_debug confirms). Every Israeli company name ends in בע"מ. The collation guide told readers to store the correct U+05F4 and never said to normalise it for search. Replaced strip_nikud() with normalize_hebrew() covering nikud + separators + geresh/gershayim, applied to BOTH sides.

Shipped SQL contradicted the prose: hebrew-search-setup.sql said non-deterministic collations 'cannot be used with UNIQUE constraints or btree indexes', the exact opposite of SKILL.md and of live behaviour. A fix is not done until every shipped script agrees with the body.

Rate-table discipline applied to a NON-rate skill: tax_config shipped employee/employer Bituach Leumi defaults of 3.50%/7.60% (two different wage bands, so they could not both be right for one salary) and INSERT ... DEFAULT VALUES materialised them into every user's DB. Removed the defaults entirely rather than picking a number, because the employee rate varies by age band, pension status and disability status. Osek patur ceiling corrected 120,000 -> 122,833 (2026, Kol Zchut).

Evidence-gate blindness worth recording: verify-evidence.py extracted only 2 facts (17%, 18%) plus 8 URLs from this skill. Almost every substantive claim here is a PostgreSQL BEHAVIOUR, which no regex can see, so a green gate proves nothing. What actually found the defects was running the SQL on a real PostgreSQL 18.6. For any developer-tools skill, stand up the real runtime.

Two evidence snippets were nav chrome or unsupported by their page (supabase-rls quoted the docs sidebar; unaccent-not-nikud attributed a U+0300-U+0362 codepoint range to a page that never mentions it). Both facts were TRUE and both citations were worthless. Re-sourced the codepoint claim to contrib/unaccent/unaccent.rules itself (99 combining-mark entries, exactly U+0300-U+0362, zero Hebrew).

A reviewer quote is not a source: a subagent supplied 'per unique user, database, and mode combination' as verbatim Supabase text for the pool-size claim. That phrase is not on the page. Caught by fetching before writing.
